direct_facts: Five fixed slots in easy 7x7 host; horizon20; actions no-op/up/down/left/right; active mask0, inactive1.
get_reward removes on goal and collision before _add_car; _add_car can reactivate a removed slot in the same environment step.
get_masks returns boundary observation mask and active/inactive mask, without per-slot generation ID or removal/arrival event list.
Uninterrupted active slots retain physical position/target/wait, while removal clears them; each reactivation assigns a spawn position and goal.
GRU runs through inactive positions; only Q output is masked. EpisodeRunner zeros hidden once per whole20-step episode.
Previous-action input also follows slot history, so source supplies no fresh-entrant hidden or previous-action boundary.
Each current active car reobserves its own target/position. Other entity visibility is distance-limited by vision1; complete recurrent state can include earlier teammate observations.
Native reward uses source distance progress, time penalty and collisions; source wait increments even for inactive slots and is not reset by every spawn.
Native spawn uses global np.random while seed() creates self.random; seeding and branch-dependent draw consumption must not be assumed from env_args seed alone.
Online and target replay unrolls both carry recurrent state across the episode, and QLearner.train issues one RMSprop.step.
inferences_and_limits: An active-to-active boundary mask does not establish uninterrupted physical-car identity.
True-survivor reset with all entrants fresh requires a declared lifetime boundary; an unmodified mask-difference adapter cannot identify all source lifetimes.

Using hidden removal/arrival callbacks as reset triggers can reveal events outside a survivor's permitted observation history via its internal-state action path; equal use by both arms is not automatically source-information preservation.
This is not an impossibility proof for a differently scoped study with common lifecycle metadata or an explicitly restricted observable event population.
A RETAIN-versus-RESET loss would at most test native cost of a memory erasure intervention; RETAIN is ordinary full causal history, not a newly established strictly-self-ancestry typed mechanism.
